concepts.definition: The condition the program is in at that moment. It is kept in a variable, and only one is valid at any time.
concepts.example: In the traffic light program, KIRMIZI, YESIL and SARI are the three states.
concepts.pitfall: Treating several state variables as independent and allowing the program to be in two states at once.

concepts.definition: The condition that triggers the move from one state to another: an event or a time running out.
concepts.example: In the KIRMIZI state, when 3000 ms are up, the program moves to YESIL.
concepts.pitfall: Not resetting the new state's time counter (`durumBasi = simdi`) during the transition; the new state ends at once.

concepts.definition: A type that gives meaningful names to numbers. It gives the first name 0 and goes on adding one for each following name.
concepts.example: Writing enum Mod { KAPALI, YAVAS, HIZLI }; makes KAPALI = 0, YAVAS = 1, HIZLI = 2.
concepts.pitfall: Writing a bare number instead of a name and hiding the meaning of the code (`durum = 2;`).

concepts.definition: A structure that runs only the matching case block depending on a variable's value. Each block ends with break;.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting break;: the program also runs the code of the next case (fall-through).

concepts.definition: Looking at the button having just become pressed, not at it "being pressed". It is done by keeping the previous state in a variable.
concepts.example: The code if (basili && !oncekiBasili) { ... } counts a press only once.
concepts.pitfall: Changing state with only the `basili` condition: a button held down jumps to the next mode every round.

quiz.prompt: In a state machine program, what is the job of the state variable?
options: It holds which state the program is in right now
It holds which pin the board is connected to
It holds the time that has passed in milliseconds
It holds how many times the button has been pressed
quiz.explanation: The state variable (for example durum or mod) holds the current state; switch looks at this value to decide which block runs. The time that has passed is kept in a separate variable (durumBasi), and the number of presses in another counter.
The mode starts at 0; at each step it becomes 1, 2, 0, 1. After 4 presses it stays at 1 (YAVAS). The % 3 operation never lets the result be 3; when it reaches 3 it goes back to 0.

quiz.prompt: A traffic light program uses these durations in its cycle: KIRMIZI 5000 ms, YESIL 4000 ms, SARI 1500 ms, then KIRMIZI again. How many milliseconds pass from the start of one red to the start of the next red?
quiz.explanation: Add up the durations of the three states: 5000 + 4000 + 1500 = 10 500 ms. When the cycle is complete, it goes back to red.

options: durumBasi = simdi; should not be written
The line digitalWrite(11, LOW); is not needed
There is no break; at the end of the KIRMIZI block
The word case YESIL: is misspelt
quiz.explanation: Because the KIRMIZI block does not end with break;, the program falls through into the YESIL block and, in the same round, turns red off and green on. So the two LEDs flicker together. Adding break; at the end of the KIRMIZI block fixes the problem. The other options are lines that work correctly.

quiz.prompt: In a state machine, what happens if the line durumBasi = simdi; is not written when moving to a new state?
options: The LEDs go off and never come back on
The program goes back to the old state and never moves on
The new state's time is worked out with the old counter, and the state can end at once
quiz.explanation: simdi - durumBasi is still worked out from the start of the old state; since the difference is already large, the new state can end one round later. There is no compile error and the program does not go back; only the durations work wrongly.
